mbm-0976.clue: Almost nobody saw my finest bow.
mbm-0976.quote: I played a tree in my first community show. I bowed so slowly after the curtain fell that a paper bird on my highest branch stayed put. The stagehand applauded from a ladder.

mbm-0977.clue: I got a birdie on the scorecard first.
mbm-0977.quote: My niece drew a little yellow bird beside my name before I teed off. When I actually sank the putt she added tail feathers. She charges by the feather now.

mbm-0978.clue: I found it by following the smell.
mbm-0978.quote: I wandered away from a tour to a cobbler’s workshop. He was polishing a pair of bright red shoes in the doorway. I came home with his directions to the best bakery and a drawing of the shoes.

mbm-0979.clue: I sometimes borrow two left hands.
mbm-0979.quote: For our school magic show my twin stood behind me and slipped his arm through my coat. We chose the same sleeve. The trick failed, but our three-handed bow brought the house down.

mbm-0980.clue: My swimming cap has a comet on it.
mbm-0980.quote: At our evening pool the lights make a patch of stars under the water. My niece painted a comet on my cap so I could swim through my very own galaxy.

mbm-0981.clue: I saved the umbrella’s little paper tag.
mbm-0981.quote: My mother picked the beach umbrella with the wide saffron stripes. From the water I could find her reading beneath it instantly. The tag marks her place in the book now.

mbm-0982.clue: Don’t polish my record off the spoon.
mbm-0982.quote: I won the pudding race at the village picnic with granddad shouting advice. He wrote my time on the prize spoon in jam. The stain is faint, but he still claims that was the family record.

mbm-0983.quote: My little cousin puts one charcoal thumbprint in my notebook for every steam engine we see. I draw wheels beneath them later. The smallest engine in the notebook has the biggest plume.

mbm-0984.quote: I built a tiny workshop beneath my robot model and painted the mechanic to look like my grandpa. Grandpa spotted the cardigan I gave him and asked why his glasses were missing.

mbm-0985.clue: I reserve one sunny patch for a photo.
mbm-0985.quote: I rest a little glass jar beside my sun lounger and wait for the blue streak of its shadow to reach my towel. When it does I take a picture and call my sister for lunch.

mbm-0986.clue: The pitcher whistles when it’s empty.
mbm-0986.quote: I pinched a little bird into the lid of my clay water jug. It doesn’t sing, but my nephew whistles for it every time I pour the last glass. He has perfect timing.

mbm-0987.clue: I turn at the smell of lemons.
mbm-0987.quote: We practice ballroom next to the kitchen at the community center. When the cook opens the oven it’s time for our last turn. I can now waltz a whole tray of lemon biscuits into existence.

mbm-0988.clue: I keep a plot secret in my desk drawer.
mbm-0988.quote: My story needed a letter that never arrived. I wrote it on a real envelope and put it in my desk drawer. Now I know exactly what the postman is hiding in chapter six.

mbm-0989.clue: I know where the lake creases.
mbm-0989.quote: Behind our towboat the water makes a little fold just before the wake flattens. I finally crossed it on one ski without shaking. Dad photographed the smile under the dripping sunglasses.

mbm-0990.clue: I check the insides of old hats.
mbm-0990.quote: A secondhand straw hat had a tiny embroidered bee tucked under the brim. I paid for the whole thing just for that secret. The bee rides every sunny bus trip with me now.

mbm-0991.clue: I let the tide carry the melody.
mbm-0991.quote: I floated my kayak past a fisherman playing a harmonica on the bank. Half the song carried downstream with me and half stayed behind. I paddled back for the ending.

mbm-0992.clue: I take two colors to the club.
mbm-0992.quote: At anime night we drew the same rocket launch in dark blue and orange pencil. I drew the tiny pair of waving hands in the window first. The engine flames could wait.

mbm-0993.clue: I threw the saucer before the cup.
mbm-0993.quote: I spent a whole pottery lesson on a saucer with a shallow spiral. My cup came out too big. My sister borrowed the saucer to serve one perfect strawberry at a time.

mbm-0994.clue: My beach towel has a little sundial.
mbm-0994.quote: I set a stick in the sand beside the corner of my towel. When its shadow points to the orange stripe, my friends know I’ll be awake for the card game.

mbm-0995.clue: I can hear the ice cream cart from two dunes away.
mbm-0995.quote: I sunbathe with one ear outside my cap. When the cart bell rings I hold the cap up like a flag. My friends put in their orders without moving from their towels.

mbm-0996.clue: My best catch was completely transparent.
mbm-0996.quote: The flying disc landed on our greenhouse roof. I stood inside and could see its bright orange circle over the tomato plants. It made a fine extra sun until Dad brought the ladder.

mbm-0997.clue: Our drummer keeps one brush in the kitchen.
mbm-0997.quote: We tried playing very quietly for a sleeping baby next door. I tapped a pie tin with a pastry brush. The baby slept and the brush got a permanent spot in our band case.

mbm-0998.clue: My first audience was a row of shirts.
mbm-0998.quote: I practiced cuatro beside the clothesline while Mum pegged out the wash. A gust made the sleeves swing in time. I finished with a bow to the blue shirt that danced the hardest.

mbm-0999.clue: I cut the toast out of felt.
mbm-0999.quote: I made my dad a tiny wool toaster for his desk. Two brown felt slices fit inside. He pushes one up every time he finishes a job he’s been putting off.

mbm-1000.clue: I picked the bench with the crooked slat.
mbm-1000.quote: The summer light leaves a zigzag across my bare foot when I sit there. I drew that little line inside my holiday journal. It takes me right back to the warmth on my ankles.
